Last week, Apple released a carrier settings update to address mobile connectivity issues encountered by some iPhone 18 Pro Max users on the AT&T network. Apple is now rolling out another, separate carrier bundle update for devices running iOS 27.2 beta. Details below.

Apple updates AT&T carrier bundle for iOS 27.2 beta

Last Friday, Apple confirmed to 9to5Mac that a small number of iPhone 18 Pro Max users on AT&T were experiencing an issue that could cause the device to lose mobile service and be unable to make calls.

Apple said that iOS 27.0.1, together with a new carrier settings update, should have prevented the issue from affecting more devices. However, iPhones that had already lost service would still require a hardware replacement.

Tonight, as spotted by Aaron Perris on X, Apple began rolling out another carrier bundle update for iPhone 18 Pro Max users on AT&T, this time specifically targeting devices running iOS 27.2 beta.

Reports of the issue first surfaced in late September, when some iPhone 18 Pro Max users on AT&T found that their devices suddenly could not make calls, send texts, or use mobile data, with the status bar only showing "SOS".

Worth noting is that the issue only affected the iPhone 18 Pro Max, which uses a Qualcomm modem in the United States. The iPhone 18 Pro, which uses the Apple C2 modem, was not affected.

The carrier settings update Apple released last week upgraded AT&T users on iOS 27.0 to version 72.1. However, users running iOS 27.2 beta were still stuck on the older 72.0.2 version of the carrier bundle.

According to reports, tonight's update bumps these devices to carrier bundle version 72.0.3, likely extending Apple's adjustments to AT&T's network to iPhone 18 Pro Max users testing the iOS 27.2 beta.
